title: Mirror Mean-Field Langevin Dynamics
claim: Respecting the constraint domain natively reaches lower loss and better particle distributions than the projection-based baseline, with or without a boundary potential.
layout: 2x3 grid; heatmap pair then loss curve per row; shared legend
description: A 2-row by 3-column grid of plots. In each row, the first two panels are triangular heatmaps of particle density over the unit simplex, drawn with a viridis colormap. The left one is Mirror MFLD and the middle one is Projected MFLD. Mirror MFLD spreads mass across the simplex and concentrates near the top vertex. Projected MFLD shows a central blob and a bright streak along one edge, which suggests mass accumulating at the boundary. The third panel in each row is a training-loss line plot against iterations from 0 to 1000. The red solid line is Mirror MFLD and the grey dashed line is Projected MFLD. The grey line drops fast but plateaus higher, while the red line ends lower. The top row is the plain setting. The bottom row adds a boundary potential. Panel titles are labelled (a) to (f).
caption: (a)-(c) MMFLD v.s. projected MFLD for optimizing a nonlinear mean-matching objective over the unit simplex; (d)-(f) with a boundary potential preventing mass accumulation.
abstract: The mean-field Langevin dynamics (MFLD) minimizes an entropy-regularized nonlinear convex functional on the Wasserstein space over $\mathbb{R}^d$, and has gained attention recently as a model for the gradient descent dynamics of interacting particle systems such as infinite-width two-layer neural networks. However, many problems of interest have constrained domains, which are not solved by existing mean-field algorithms due to the global diffusion term. We study the optimization of probability measures constrained to a convex subset of $\mathbb{R}^d$ by proposing the \emph{mirror mean-field Langevin dynamics} (MMFLD), an extension of MFLD to the mirror Langevin framework. We obtain linear convergence guarantees for the continuous MMFLD via a uniform log-Sobolev inequality, and uniform-in-time propagation of chaos results for its time- and particle-discretized counterpart.
